claim.claim-text: 1. A system to control glycemia in a patient, the system comprising: a controller configured to:

receive glucose data at intervals, determine a glucose target, execute a model-predictive controller algorithm to predict physiological glucose values and to solve an objective function for an optimal insulin trajectory, the objective function comprising a sum of weighted differences between the predicted physiological glucose and the glucose target, determine the dose request from the optimal insulin trajectory, and transmit the dose request.
2. The system of claim 1, further comprising: an insulin delivery device for delivering insulin to the patient, in response to the dose request.

3. The system of claim 1 or 2, further comprising: a glucose measurement device in communication with the controller and for measuring the glucose data, including a glucose concentration, in the patient.
4. The system of any of the claims 1 to 3, wherein the weighting is applied by applying a weighting function to the differences between the predicted physiological glucose and glucose target.
5. The system of claim 4, wherein through the weighting function a weighting factor is determined for every difference between the predicted physiological glucose and glucose target.
6. The system according to any of the preceding claims, wherein the objective function and the weighting depend on one or more of the following: time since meal, meal size, and exercise level.
7. The system according to any of the preceding claims, wherein the weighting increases with time after a meal up to a constant weighting at a predetermined period after a meal.
8. The system according to any of the preceding claims, wherein the glucose target is a function of a prescribed target glucose level, exercise, or time after meal.
9. The system according to any of the preceding claims, wherein the objective function further comprises the sum of basal deviations from the basal insulin profile.
10. The system according to the preceding claim, wherein the basal deviations are squared and weighted.
11. The system of claim 9 or 10, wherein the summed values in the sum of basal deviations from the basal insulin profile are weighted differently based on time from a meal.

12. The system according to any of the preceding claims, wherein the weightings in the sum of weighted differences between the predicted physiological glucose and the glucose target are a function of time or vary with time after a meal.

13. The system according to any of the preceding claims, wherein the differences between the predicted physiological glucose and the glucose target are squared in the sum of weighted differences between the predicted physiological glucose and the glucose target.
